Thanks,

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Spike in 5xxs this morning - urgent

Quick triage notes (first pass):
- Observed elevated 429 + 5xx across the US-west frontends starting ~13:37 PST, peaked ~13:44.
- Backend error rate is correlated with a bursty ingress pattern: many identical client IPs reattempting rapidly.
- Trace attached shows repeated immediate retries with minimal spacing (ingress_traces_1103.zip).
- No config push on our side at that time; autoscaler was healthy.

Likely hypothesis: client-side retry behavior caused request fanout when a subset of upstream pods briefly degraded (latency spike). This looks like a classic retry amplification — immediate retries without jitter.

Immediate ask: if ProdEdge can disable client retries or reduce them to 1 while we apply a short-term server-side throttle, that will reduce pressure.

(Attachment: ingress_traces_1103.zip)
—Ben
Ben Carter | SRE (on-call) | Redwood Inference
From: Lily Tran <lily.tran@prodedge.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 15:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xxs this morning - urgent

Folks — we’re running SDK v1.2 (prodedge-client-java:1.2.0) in several services. We just confirmed the default retry policy there is 5 immediate retries (no jitter/backoff) when a request returns 429/5xx. We haven’t changed concurrency.

We can flip a feature flag to reduce retries but that requires a canary which will take ~90 minutes. If you can throttle on your side first, we’ll follow with SDK changes.

Lily
Lily Tran | Platform Reliability | ProdEdge Systems
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Proposed mitigation — ProdEdge 5xx fanout

Team — summary and recommended actions:
- Root cause (likely): ProdEdge SDK default retry policy (5 immediate retries, no jitter) amplified a transient latency event into a request fanout → overloaded some backends → increased 5xx/429.

Short-term mitigation (apply within 15–30 min):
1) Enable server-side token-bucket throttle at the edge for ProdEdge API key (cap burst to current baseline + 20%).
2) Apply soft circuit-breaker: if a backend pod experiences >25% 5xx over 1m, route new requests to region fallback/queue with 10s smoothing.
3) Temporarily raise ProdEdge quota by 15% for the next 2 hours to allow retries that do happen to succeed while throttling prevents amplification.
4) Add a request-level 200ms acknowledgement for long-pending requests to avoid cascading client retries.

Medium-term: request ProdEdge roll-forward to SDK v1.3 which includes exponential backoff + jitter; we’ll provide a patch and a sample config. Also add a customer-facing KB on safe retry patterns.

I’ve drafted a mitigation playbook (mitigation_playbook_5xx_fanout.md) — pushing it to Confluence and the incident ticket. Ben/Evelyn please action 1–3 and confirm once live. Monica — coordinate communications with ProdEdge and confirm SDK rollout ETA.

— Karthik
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@prodedge.com>, Lily Tran <lily.tran@prodedge.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xxs this morning - urgent

Samir / Lily — quick update and next steps: we implemented the edge token-bucket throttle and soft circuit-breaker at 18:20 UTC last night; error rate dropped from ~30% to <3% within 12 minutes. We also applied a temporary 15% quota increase for the burst window.

ProdEdge agreed to a rapid SDK patch: they will enable exponential backoff with randomized jitter and reduce immediate retries to 1 in a staged canary (ETA: 24 hours).

Deliverables:
- We created INC-4129 with the playbook and traces linked: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4129
- Customer patch (prodedge-client-java v1.3.1) will be validated in their canary tomorrow morning.
- Follow-up: schedule a joint postmortem (internal + ProdEdge) for Friday to capture mitigations and add a KB entry for recommended client retry configurations.

Thanks for the quick coordination everyone — outreach to the execs has been done and CS will update the account dashboard.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
